newsitem.title: USA: Aer Lingus launches Newark summer service.
newsitem.headline: Aer Lingus launches Newark summer service.

text.p: Aer Lingus said it will begin its first service from Dublin and Shannon to Newark International on May 15, using an all-economy Lockheed L-1011-50 Tristar leased from UK-based Caledonian Airways.
The summer service will operate daily except for Tuesdays, Aer Lingus spokesman, Jim Lyndon told Reuters. Caledonian will provide the flight crew and Aer Lingus the cabin crew.

No cargo space will be sold on the flights as the existing and planned capacity offered by services to Kennedy airport as well as to Boston and Chicago's O'Hare is sufficient, the carrier's Dublin spokesman, Declan Conroy said.

Aer Lingus operates Airbus Industrie A330-300 aircraft on its 16 weekly flights to Kennedy from Ireland with eight flying direct and the remainder stopping in Shannon, offering around 10 tonnes of capacity per flight.
Conroy said cargo business to and from North America was going very well.

The carrier is also increasing A330-300 services from Ireland to Chicago to six a week by the start of June following the launch of a fourth flight in April. Each flight will offer around eight tonnes of cargo capacity, Conroy said.
The airline has four A330-3OOs and a fifth, two year-old plane, is being acquired from the manufacturer, Airbus Industrie in time to help expand the Chicago service, he added.
At present the carrier also provides a once weekly McDonnell Douglas-8-63F freighter flight to Chicago with 30 tonnes of capacity.

This is leased from Dublin-based Aer Turas and will be withdrawn at end-May as the 48 tonnes combined capacity on the six passenger flights will be similar to that of the DC-8 and three A330 flights, he said.

Aer Lingus will also provide a daily Dublin-Boston flight from June 1, using the A330s but offering 10 tonnes cargo capacity due to the lower fuel requirements compared to the Chicago flights, Conroy added. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
